d95.len.again.text: There they are. Sit, sit. Kim, another coffee over here.

d95.mary.again.text: You're in my light again. Sit. The bars are still lemon.

d95.len.thanks.text: That's the crib. That's it exactly. And a casing, standing up like that. They'll go right up front at the open house. Thank you.

d95.len.east.ask.text: Anything east of Bald Eagle? Gull, Pietro?

d95.lead.pads.text: Tauno: up the grade from the crews' landing to the west pads. The big one's in a hollow, the Kettle. Go after a rain and see if the creek still runs orange.

d95.und.backdoor.text: Pietro. The hill E-7 was filed on.

d95.S7.rose.again.text: There you are. Sit down, I saved you the chair. What's the lake doing?

d95.S7.page.rose.text: Rose Gornik. Tuesdays at Moose Lake, the table by the window. She wants June lilacs for the church calendar.

d95.S7.page.whose.text: Her family's resort was on the big part of Basswood. Bought out in '64, burned on the ice the next February.

d95.S7.page.where.text: Lilacs past Prairie, on the US side of the bay. An old Finn fish camp. The boys there called the old lady Mummo.

d95.S7.page.boys.text: The boys were Haapalas. The young one drowned. The other one guided. Walt.

d95.S7.page.step.text: Three flat stones up from the water to nothing. A foundation in the grass. Somebody's lilacs.

d95.S9.page.hooked.text: Off the Alice beach rock, a jig dragged on the sand caught something heavy. Not a fish.

d95.S9.page.nb06.text: Coffee Lake is Alice. Walt lost something off the beach rock in '88, in eight feet of water.

d95.S9.end.text: It came up by the bail. A blue enamel pot, a chip on the lip, full of sand.

d95.kettle.page.done.text: Worked the Kettle creek with Tasha. Three bottles and the disk. The water's orange-brown under a metre.

d95.beat.whitestone.text: There's a white stone on a flat rock at a site on Bald Eagle. Somebody put it there. We left it.

95:stream-r-the-run.1.text: Far off, down toward the bay: a radio, two clicks.

95:stream-r-the-run.2.text: Tied off in the canoe · cold, cramped

c.walt.n42.text: Not with company on the lake.

d95.7a.S2.page.duane.text: Duane, the Tattler. Weekends in the lot at Moose River North: a green pickup, a lawn chair, a plaster cast.

d95.7a.S2.page.site.text: The west site on Big Moose, under the ridge. Two stars, a bad landing. Nobody wants it.

d95.7a.S2.page.walt.text: Walt slept out there in his canoe, tied to a snag off the point.

d95.7a.S2.page.night.text: Two in the morning on Big Moose. Steps on the ridge, a knock on wood, twice. Then nothing for a minute.

d95.7a.S2.page.tracks.text: In the morning, up on the ridge: a moose and a calf, and the serviceberry stripped.

d95.7a.S2.page.frame.text: One picture from 2:04. Two birches, and something between them. Nothing there by day.

d95.7a.S2.end.solved.text: A moose in the deadfall and a bear in the berries. Duane ran it anyway.

d95.7a.S2.end.kept.text: Kept the picture. Haven't shown anybody.

d95.7a.S2.wake.text: Two in the morning. You come awake. Something heavy on the ridge behind the tent.

d95.7a.S2.charge.text: The cow lays her ears back, stamps, and comes three strides at you. Then she's gone, crashing.

d95.7a.S2.eyes.text: Two eyes in the lamp, green-gold, two metres up. Then a long face. Then they go.

d95.7a.S2.cast.text: Bear. Hind foot over the front.

d95.7a.S3.page.elaine.text: Elaine Sundquist keeps the sky book at Slim. Everything's something, she says.

d95.7a.S3.page.aurora.text: Northern lights over Fourtown, low in the north. In the book.

d95.7a.S3.page.train.text: A string of lights climbing out of the west, one after another. Satellites. In the book.

d95.7a.S3.page.lantern.text: A light floating at the north end in the fog. Somebody's lantern. In the book.

d95.7a.S3.page.foxfire.text: Foxfire off the north shore, a green chunk of birch. Elaine turned the shop lights off for it.

d95.7a.S3.page.square.text: Walt wrote in her book in 2012. 'Kept the red on.' She wrote 'boat?' beside it.

d95.7a.S3.page.tin.text: Under the loose stone at the long rock: a tobacco tin. Red glass in oilcloth, three matches.

d95.7a.S3.page.one.text: A light over the north bay. Low, steady. It drifted against the wind and went out when I showed white.

d95.7a.S3.end.text: Elaine wrote a question mark in red. Her first.

d95.7a.S4.page.kari.text: Kari Vang counts wolves on Agnes. Three places, three lines, they cross where the wolves are.

d95.7a.S4.page.tracks.text: Kari at the landing: front foot, toes tight, like it's going somewhere. A dog's go everywhere.

d95.7a.S4.page.st1.text: Nina Moose, the north end, three in the morning. They answered.

d95.7a.S4.page.st3.text: Walt's site on Agnes, the sand landing. They answered.

d95.7a.S4.page.ring.text: The three lines cross west of Agnes, in the primitive area.

d95.7a.S4.page.kill.text: Ravens over a kill. A deer, mostly hair and bones.

d95.7a.S4.page.count.text: The meadow from the ridge at dusk. Pups at the edge of the alders.

d95.7a.S4.page.told.text: I told someone where the meadow is.

d95.7a.S4.pay.station.text: $15 from Kari, a night at a station.

d95.7a.S4.lyle2.text: Me again. Sixty-five for a ring on my map. Last time I'll ask.

d95.7a.S4.give.text: Show him the ring on the map.

d95.7a.S4.howl.hint.text: Wait for an answer. Face it, then {E} Mark.

95:a3-the-guiding-years.11.text: Tow landing Flat rock on the point Old fire ring, under the moss Pine stub

95:a3-the-guiding-years.14.text: The old guide photo? Little Gabbro? Bald Eagle? Hap says Insula? Hap says Ottertrack? The Stuart Portage?

d95.s1.page.1.text: Ollie. Walks the Stuart Portage Tuesdays and Thursdays, in the evening. Says "Evening."

d95.s1.page.2.text: Rescue squad, 38 years. Squad record on the Stuart: 49 minutes, canoe and pack, one trip. 1981.

d95.s1.page.3.text: He'll be at the road with his watch.

d95.s1.page.missed.text: Over forty-nine. He said Tuesday like it was nothing.

d95.s1.page.beat.text: Road to river under forty-nine. He looked at the watch twice.

d95.s1.page.twice.text: Carried it twice. Never under forty-nine. He seemed fine with that.

d95.s1.page.log.text: He gave me a copy of his search log. Bald Eagle, October 1977. Nine days.

d95.s8.page.1.text: A sled on the lunch rock, Insula. Ash runners, the straps rusted to lace. Two window sashes, one pane left.

d95.s8.page.rule.text: Tom's rule: over fifty years old, it stays. Under, it goes.

d95.s8.page.crew.text: His crew is on Insula the third week of September. If nobody tells him anything, it goes.

d95.s8.page.emil.text: Emil. Trapped Insula from the thirties. Went back over the ice for his windows and left the sled on the rock.

d95.s8.page.creek.text: His creek: straight across from the rock. A beaver house at the mouth.

d95.s8.page.snap.text: Lloyd's snapshot: Vern with a pike on the sled, 1968. Both panes in.

d95.s8.page.found.text: Up the creek in the young pines: cut stumps, a stovepipe, a square hollow, a bed spring.

d95.s8.page.tin.text: A tobacco tin under the spring. E.R. 1947.

d95.s8.end.heritage.text: The sled stays. Tom wrote it up as heritage.

d95.s8.photo.sled.text: the sled on the lunch rock

d95.p.blade.offer.text: That a shovel blade? Somebody's, once. Twenty bucks for the wall, if you're not attached to it.

d95.p.m.register.text: The bunkhouse register. W. Helstrom, day use, parked.

d95.p.m.receipt.text: A fuel receipt from the camp on the Isabella.

d95.p.m.guestbook.text: Aili's guest book. He signed it.

d95.p.m.tasha.text: Somebody at the company flagged the stations last year.

d95.p.m.tauno.text: There's a man who'll go on the record.

d95.p.m.creek.text: A picture of the orange creek.

d95.p.m.farend.text: I think I know where it is.

d95.p.cig.text: A cigarette butt, still warm. A brand band on it.

d95.p.m.wadenum.text: That number Denny gave me. It's Wade's.
